class CondHelpController < ApplicationController
  def destroy
    ensure_owner! unless params[:shared]
    Note.find(params[:id]).destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def purge
    params[:force] || ensure_owner!
    Note.find(params[:id]).destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def archive
    @note = Note.find(params[:id])
    check_owner! if params[:strict]
    @note.update!(archived: true)
    head :no_content
  end

  def twin
    ensure_owner!
    Note.find(params[:id]).destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  private

  def ensure_owner!
    current_user.notes.find(params[:id])
  end

  def check_owner!
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @note.user == current_user
  end
end

expect.why: `ensure_owner! unless params[:shared]`: the helper's scoped find runs only without ?shared; inline() walks the whole statement and runs it unconditionally, verifying the id
`params[:force] || ensure_owner!` short-circuits the check
`check_owner! if params[:strict]`: the helper's raise refusal is credited although it runs only with ?strict
twin: the helper runs unconditionally

class CondShapesController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_note

  def destroy
    begin
      @note.archive!
    rescue Archive::Error
      require_owner!
    end
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def purge
    case @note.status
    in "locked" then require_owner!
    in _ then nil
    end
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def loop_check
    while params[:confirm] == "yes"
      require_owner!
      break
    end
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  def twin
    require_owner!
    @note.destroy
    head :no_content
  end

  private

  def set_note
    @note = Note.find(params[:id])
  end

  def require_owner!
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @note.user == current_user
  end
end

expect.why: the check runs only in a `rescue` clause of a `begin` block (when archiving fails); `rescue` isn't in _conditional_at's list, so the inlined raise reads as unconditional
pattern matching: `case … in "locked" then require_owner!` checks only locked notes; `case_match`/`in_clause` aren't in the list
a `while` loop body runs only while the condition holds; only the modifier forms are listed
twin: the check runs unconditionally
